short_answer: Bryan Power is an active pick seller on WagerTalk, a Las Vegas marketplace with written terms and a refund policy. His page was updated on 17 Nov 2026 and sells single plays, short passes and a one year pass.

Whether the picks make money over time is not shown in any full record we could open. The page leads with "NOW UP 93.1 UNITS ~ IN ALL SPORTS ~ SINCE APRIL!" and "24-10 (70%) RUN WITH ALL FOOTBALL!", streaks that start where the seller chose. The Last 20 table on the same page showed 9 wins and 11 losses when we counted it.
We found very few independent buyer posts about him. The few we found were neutral or mildly positive. Treat him as an established but unproven seller and record every pick yourself.
pricing_intro: All prices below were on the Bryan Power WagerTalk page on 17 Nov 2026. WagerTalk shows a higher list price next to most sale prices; we give both. The All Access passes on the page are WagerTalk passes, and the page does not say they cover only his picks.

guarantee: The guarantee is an extra you pay for. A $5.00 play costs $8.00 with it. WagerTalk says the option "backs your purchase with 100% in credits" and applies if the package "does not result in an overall profit across all included plays." The paid amount comes back as account credit for a future purchase, not as cash.

The WagerTalk refund policy says "All Sales are Final and products are sold “as is”" and that no refund is issued once a product has been purchased, delivered or viewed. The site terms add that the buyer's exclusive remedy is a refund of the price paid or replacement of the product, at WagerTalk's option. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

What the seller publishes: streak totals, leaderboard entries such as 33-22-2 (60%) over the last 30 days, and a Last 20 table. WagerTalk grades these itself and also sells the picks.

A third party: GameAdvisers, a site that says it may earn sportsbook commissions, tracks his free WagerTalk picks. On 17 Nov 2026 it showed 9-6 and +$246 over the last 30 days, while another box on the same page said 9-7. That covers free picks only, a sample of about 15 plays, and the profit figures seem to assume a flat $100 win on every price.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Bryan Power pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Bryan Power performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the streaks on his page run from about 60% to 82% winners, while his Last 20 table showed 45%. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Bryan Power is thin. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found only a few independent posts about Bryan Power: a 2013 Sportsbook Review tally of free picks that put him on top at 12 wins and 5 losses, and 2026 TheRX threads where members repost WagerTalk plays without results. No buyer complaint, and no detailed buyer praise of his paid packages, turned up in our searches. Apart from WagerTalk's own streaks, the only tracking we found covers his free picks.

In an SBR thread comparing handicappers' free picks from early Feb to late Mar 2013, one member who kept a tally said Bryan Power was the best of the group at 12 wins and 5 losses, up 5.6 units. That covered free picks only, not paid packages.

TheRX lists all WagerTalk handicappers among the services members may not post in its daily service play threads, so his paid plays are rarely shared and checked there. We found no buyer post on TheRX describing his results.

Web searches found no Covers, SBR or TheRX thread reviewing his paid packages, no Trustpilot or Better Business Bureau page and no court or regulator record. Our Reddit archive search for him could not finish on 17 Nov 2026 because the archive was overloaded, so this page has no Reddit posts.

conflicts: WagerTalk sells his picks, grades his record, writes his bio and runs the leaderboard that ranks him. None of those numbers is independent of the seller.
GameAdvisers, the only outside tracker we found, describes him as part of the WagerTalk Group and carries an affiliate disclosure for sportsbook partners.
TheRX lists "All Wagertalk Cappers" among the services members may not post in its daily service play threads. The rule does not say why, and it says nothing about the quality of the picks.
strengths: Sold through a marketplace with a named Las Vegas seller address, written terms and a refund policy.
Prices are published for every play and pass, and single plays were on sale for $5.
The page shows a Last 20 table with losses as well as wins, and his free picks are tracked by an outside site.
concerns: No full public record of paid picks. Every headline number is a streak chosen by the seller.
The guarantee costs extra and pays in site credit, never cash. All sales are final.
Very few independent buyer posts exist, good or bad.
Some bio numbers are years old, such as the April and May 2022 run.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, active seller on WagerTalk, a Las Vegas marketplace with written terms, and his page was updated on 17 Nov 2026. We could not verify that his paid picks win over time, because no full record is published, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Bryan Power cost?

On 17 Nov 2026 single plays were $5.00 ($8.00 with the guarantee), short passes were $49.00, and a one year pass was $1,188.00. WagerTalk all access passes ran from $39.00 for a day to $1,999.00 for a year.
Does Bryan Power have a verified record?
No. The page shows streaks such as up 93.1 units since April, graded by WagerTalk. An outside site tracks only his free picks, about 15 of them over the last 30 days.

Plays are cheap at $5, but nothing shows the paid picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays. The guarantee only returns site credit, and your betting losses are never covered.
